resources.string: Choose what WhoCaller can use. You can change this any time in Settings. Everything you skip can be turned on later.

WhoCaller asks Android to make it your caller ID & spam app. Android then shows WhoCaller the number of incoming calls from people who aren\'t in your contacts, so it can identify them and warn you about suspected spam. WhoCaller can\'t listen to or record calls. On Android 9 and older, this uses the phone state permission instead.
Without this, WhoCaller can\'t identify or block calls as they arrive. You can still search numbers manually.
Used to display your recent calls.
WhoCaller reads your call log on this device to show recent calls with caller names and spam labels. Your call history is never uploaded.
Recent calls won\'t be shown. Caller ID and search still work.
Used to identify numbers already saved on your device.
WhoCaller checks your contacts on this device so people you know are never labelled as unknown or spam. Your contacts are not uploaded to WhoCaller servers.
Saved contacts can\'t be recognised, and \"Block unknown callers\" stays off.
Used for caller alerts and spam warnings.
WhoCaller shows who is calling and warns you about suspected spam using notifications. You can switch individual alert types off in Settings.
You won\'t see caller alerts during calls.
Used to call and video call directly from WhoCaller.

Lets WhoCaller place calls when you tap Call, and check whether your SIM and carrier support video calling so the Video call button only appears when it will work. WhoCaller never calls anyone without you tapping Call.
Calls open in your phone app instead, and video calling is hidden.
Use WhoCaller for all calls: caller name before it rings, full-screen incoming calls, in-call controls and video calls.
Use WhoCaller for text messages, with scam warnings on suspicious texts.
Select WhoCaller in the list that opens.
